column1: At a four-colour vertex after the bends, `κ(θ + 60°) = κ̄(θ)` wherever both are defined (`κ`: ring tile colour, or an (R2) arc's inner colour)

**The window lemma**: at a `κ`-change point `y` (`Ā | A`), if `κ` is defined just beyond `y + 60°`, the window `(y, y + 60°)` carries no `Ā` and all its `A`-contacts are one tile, which reaches `y + 60°` (a change point when `κ` is defined just before it too); mirror for `(y − 60°, y)`
A four-colour vertex whose ring carries no (Q) arc has ring change points exactly `y + 60°ℤ`: six ring tiles alternating the absent colours, each spanning a closed 60° arc

**No pinwheel has a ring free of (Q) arcs** (after the bends); in particular none with a `Γ`-free ring, at radius `1 + ε`. *(Stage 2's added clause "and the pinwheel `α ≡ 90°`" is withdrawn: N6-QOUT admits (Q) arcs there.)* Proof corrected in §3.1: a 60° cone forces the next cone below 120° (N6-P60′), so all four would be 60°
K1-PIN after stage 3: the pinwheel is excluded at radius `1 + ε` unless its ring carries (Q) arcs of N6-QOUT's kind; **GAP** there

*(Stage 2's N6-P60, "a 60° cone is impossible", is withdrawn: its step 1 misread the Reuleaux triangle's corner cone as 60°; it is 120°.)* If `α_{j+1} = 60°` and `κ` is defined on the two 60° windows beside `q_j`, then `T_{j+2}` reaches `q_j`, lies in `Reul(p, q_j, q_{j+1})`, borders the whole side `e_{j+1}` from `p` to `q_j`, and `α_{j+1} + α_{j+2} < 180°`

A (Q) arc on the pinwheel's ring has inner `T_{j+1}`, lies in `[φ_j − min(60°, 180° − α_{j+1}), φ_j + min(0, α_{j+1} + α_{j+2} − 180°)]`, and has outer colour `c_{j+3}` (outer `c_j`, `c_{j+2}` impossible by U1)

If `α_{j+1} ∈ (60°, 120°)`, no (Q) arc of `T_{j+2}` (outer colour `c_j`) holds `e(φ_j + 60°)` inside: `ω(q_j)` would enter a `c_j`-tile (N-E1 at `q_j`, which carries `c_j` by `z_j`); the pinwheel `α ≡ 90°` with full-zone (Q) arcs dies
In the pinwheel every cone satisfies `60° ≤ α_j < 180°`: a 180° cone would put `T_{j+1}`'s sector outside `B̄(q_j, 1)` beside `e_{j+1}`

At a non-Siamese degree-4 vertex whose ring carries no (Q) arc (after the bends), all tactic centres lie in one class mod 60°: every cone between tactic edges is a multiple of 60°, and a lens is Reuleaux or `γ = 0°`; **non-Reuleaux lenses need a (Q) arc**

At a tactic centre that is a change point with `κ` defined on both windows beside it, the directions toward `p` are covered only by `p`'s own tiles reaching it; a unit gap between consecutive centres of one tile pushes that tile aside and forces a neighbour into a Reuleaux triangle on `p`

For every `K`, a valid map in `𝓜_K` has a stationary random valid map in its hull whose Palm version is unimodular and hyperfinite, so of average curvature zero (Euler in expectation, pinch points included by multiplicity); route T's counts and N3-JOINT's assignment (a mass transport) hold as intensity identities: the aperiodic averaging step for Q-full_K closes by printed theorems; GAP-μ, K1, K2-loc, the Siamese class and unbounded complexity are untouched
